clue.text: Not even time for some breakfast cereal?

parts.note: a surface that is not even is rough
an age is a long stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a lumpy, slow-to-prepare cereal leaves no time for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: bran cereal is eaten for its fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibre-rich cereal is eaten precisely to supply bulk in the diet, so it serves as an example of dietary fibre.

clue.text: Reported old area of land poorly cultivated

indicators.note: reported speech is heard, so the word for the land measure is said aloud

parts.note: a rood is an old British measure of land, a quarter of an acre

explanation.surface: A report on an old plot of farmland that has been badly tended.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude in its older sense means rough and unrefined, as of land or manners left unpolished.

clue.text: In the lead, when discovering exotic tree

parts.note: a team in the lead is up
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A plant hunter takes the lead on finding a rare tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovering' is a link word here. The upas is a Javanese tree famed for its poisonous sap.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a tropical Asian tree of legend whose sap was used to poison arrows.

clue.text: Massive explosive nuclear disaster

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

indicators.note: a disaster leaves the letters of the next word wrecked and scattered

explanation.surface: A huge blast follows a catastrophe at a nuclear plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive' looks like it describes the nuclear disaster, but it gives HE; 'disaster' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean tasks are enormous, named after the mythical strongman, so the word means huge in scale or effort.

clue.text: Committee's turn, perhaps, to be ignored

definitions.meaning: a board is a committee, and its go is its turn: read cryptically, the board's go
an idiom for being abandoned or disregarded

explanation.surface: A committee member's slot on the agenda is quietly passed over.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be discarded or neglected, originally of things falling overboard from a ship.

clue.text: Order that is given for attack

parts.note: to sort is to put in order
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A commander issues the order to launch an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a sally by troops from a defended position, a sudden attack.

clue.text: What's round and long, say?

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape
to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: A riddle asks what thing is both circular and lengthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, which is to say what one thinks.

clue.text: Standard sort of telephone switchboard originally installed

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a touchtone telephone is the push-button kind

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word switchboard

explanation.surface: An engineer describes the standard type of phone and the switchboard first put in.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the first letter of 'switchboard', is placed inside TOUCHTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A touchstone was a stone for testing gold, hence any criterion or benchmark.

clue.text: Route, perhaps, a French chap's taken up as a way home?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Len is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's route back is described as a sort of road home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns ROUTE into EUROT; 'taken up' turns LEN into NEL. The question mark marks the definition: for travellers to Britain, the Channel Tunnel is a way home.
explanation.definitionFit: The tunnel under the Channel is the rail route by which travellers return from France to Britain.

clue.text: Criticism people got after returning to help

indicators.note: after places the people piece behind the other
returning means the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid is help
a tribe is a people

explanation.surface: A community is censured after coming back to offer assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a forceful piece of criticism.

clue.text: Someone having a taste, say, for booze

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, so it is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a licker is someone who licks, taking a taste

explanation.surface: A drinker sampling something is asked whether they fancy alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is alcoholic drink, spirits especially, which is what booze is slang for.

clue.text: Hamlet's traditionally natural character

parts.note: not the Prince of Denmark: a hamlet is a small settlement, and a natural is an old word for a simpleton, a stock figure of rural life

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet' tempts towards Shakespeare, but the capital is only there because it starts the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock figure of rural life is the simple-minded local, once called a natural.

clue.text: Right before giving the talk I, foolishly, appeared offhand

indicators.note: before puts this piece ahead of the next

parts.note: just means right or fair

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the letters are arranged in a silly way

explanation.surface: Someone right before giving a speech seemed casual and dismissive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges THE TALK I into LIKETHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something done casually and without fuss, which is what an offhand manner is.

clue.text: Fortunate outcome after questionable change of leadership

indicators.note: a change of leadership swaps the first letter of the word for another

parts.note: something questionable is suspicious

explanation.surface: After a dubious coup, the result turned out well.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening S of SUSPICIOUS is replaced by A; 'outcome after' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Auspicious means favourable or promising good luck, so lucky.

clue.text: Article in packages useless for an alchemist

indicators.note: in places the article within the packages

parts.note: parcels are packages
a is the indefinite article
US is shorthand for unserviceable, useless

explanation.surface: Someone finds an item in parcels that is no good to a medieval alchemist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'useless' gives US, old military slang for unserviceable.
explanation.definitionFit: Paracelsus was a sixteenth-century Swiss physician famed for his alchemical work.

clue.text: Custom country, say, rejected

parts.note: the USA is a country

indicators.note: rejected means the abbreviation is turned back

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A nation's tradition is said to have been spurned.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means established practice or habit, a synonym for custom.

clue.text: Leader of band heading off commander of armed forces

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington commanded the British army against Napoleon

explanation.surface: A bandleader cuts off the head of a military commander.
explanation.walkthrough: WELLINGTON loses its first letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington was the celebrated American jazz bandleader and composer.

clue.text: Teen love taking time to develop into short romance

indicators.note: to develop is to change shape and grow, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teenage crush takes time to blossom into a brief love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' adds T to TEENLOVE; 'to develop' rearranges all nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel, typically a light romantic story.

clue.text: Flat note no good for church music

parts.note: plain land is flat
so (soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer's flat note is no good for a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied medieval chant used in church liturgy.

clue.text: Roads without verges meet here

indicators.note: verges are edges, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: avenues are roads

explanation.surface: Roads with no grass edges come together at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: AVENUES loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue is the place where people gather or an event is held.

clue.text: Conservative woman leads candidates contesting seat

indicators.note: leads puts the woman's piece ahead of the next

parts.note: Hester is a woman's name
the field is all those competing

explanation.surface: A Tory woman heads the field of candidates fighting for a parliamentary seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chesterfield is a padded leather sofa, a kind of seat.

clue.text: Nail-biting future, maybe

definitions.meaning: the future is one example of a grammatical verb form

explanation.surface: Anxious waiting about what is to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense means strained and anxious; also the grammatical category of verbs marking time, like past or future.

clue.text: Determined in business

explanation.surface: Someone resolute in commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means resolute and unyielding; as a noun it is a commercial company.

clue.text: Stomach or shoulder

definitions.meaning: to shoulder is to carry a burden

explanation.surface: Two parts of the body side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear is to put up with something and also to carry its weight, as one shoulders a load.

clue.text: Duke's ancestors in old houses

indicators.note: the words house the answer, holding it inside them

explanation.surface: A nobleman's forebears lived in ancient family homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' tells you the answer is inside 'ancestors in old'. Orsino is the Duke in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino is the Duke of Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Small zip I sent for repair

indicators.note: something sent for repair will be taken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A broken zip is posted off to be mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Pint-size is an informal word for tiny, like something holding only a pint.

clue.text: Way to produce extremely saucy, short epigram

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extremes, the first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: A recipe for writing a cheeky, brief witticism.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the first and last letters of 'saucy', 'short' and 'epigram' gives SY, ST, EM. 'short' looks like a description of the epigram but is a source word.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is a method or way of doing something.

clue.text: Flag shown by vessel queen's boarded

indicators.note: something that has boarded a ship is inside it

parts.note: a steamer is a ship
R, for Regina, is the Latin abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A ship flies a pennant when the monarch comes aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside STEAMER; 'queen's' is 'queen has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant flown from a mast.
